#Desktop integration

Wren is one portable executable with no installer. The desktop integration is what makes it part of the user's desktop anyway: a launcher in the application menu, its icon, and the registration as a program that can open web addresses. It is added and removed by one switch, in the user's own profile, never system-wide and never with administrator rights.

Where: the box Integrate Wren with the desktop at the top of about:config (and the command of the same name in the palette). Its state is read from the disk every time it is shown, never from a preference, so it is always true.

StateThe boxMeaning
absentuntickednone of the files exists
installedtickedevery file exists and runs this executable
to repairticked, with a notepoints to <path> - Update: the files run another executable (Wren was moved, or updated into another folder); incomplete - Repair: some files are missing

#Windows

Everything is in HKEY_CURRENT_USER and the user's Start menu folder.

  • %APPDATA%\Microsoft\Windows\Start Menu\Programs\Wren.lnk, made with IShellLinkW and IPersistFile: the executable, its own icon, its folder as working directory, and the AppUserModelID FromentSoftware.Wren (IPropertyStore, PKEY_AppUserModel_ID). The program sets the same ID for its windows (SetCurrentProcessExplicitAppUserModelID, before the first window), so pinning the shortcut to the taskbar and grouping the windows under it work.

  • Registration as a candidate browser. Windows does not let a program make itself the default browser: the user picks one in Settings > Apps > Default apps (the box has a button that opens that page).

    • Software\Clients\StartMenuInternet\Wren (name, icon, command, Capabilities with the URL associations http and https and the file associations of browser.desktop_integration.file_types)
    • Software\RegisteredApplications, value Wren
    • Software\Classes\WrenHTML, the ProgID, whose shell\open\command is "<exe>" "%1"
    • then SHChangeNotify(SHCNE_ASSOCCHANGED).
  • Development builds use Wren Dev, WrenDev, FromentSoftware.Wren.Dev: they never touch the release's entries.

Removal deletes the shortcut when it carries the AppUserModelID or runs the executable, the keys that hold the WrenIntegration mark or run the executable, and the RegisteredApplications value that names Wren's Capabilities key. Nothing else: the user's choices (UserChoice), other programs' keys, a Wren.lnk that is not Wren's all stay.

#Linux

  • $XDG_DATA_HOME/applications/wren.desktop (~/.local/share/applications by default): Type, Name, Exec (quoted as the Desktop Entry Specification says, %U), TryExec, Icon, Categories=Network;WebBrowser;, MimeType= for x-scheme-handler/http, x-scheme-handler/https and the file types, and the marker X-Wren-Integration=wren. update-desktop-database runs afterwards when installed. The entry passes desktop-file-validate.
  • $XDG_DATA_HOME/icons/hicolor/<n>x<n>/apps/wren.png for the sizes Wren embeds (16, 32, 64, 256, 512).

#macOS

Not provided: what macOS lists is an application bundle, and Wren is an executable outside any bundle. See src/desktop/integration_darwin.odin.

#Parts, and what the options map to

The integration is a set of parts; install writes the ones the options ask for and takes away the ones they do not (that is what Modify does); remove takes away every part that carries Wren's mark.

PartOption in SetupWindowsLinux
LauncherAdd to Start menuWren.lnk in the Start menuthe .desktop file
Desktop shortcutCreate desktop shortcuta second .lnk (same AppUserModelID) in the Desktop foldernot provided
RegistrationRegister as a web browserthe StartMenuInternet / ProgID keys aboveMimeType= in the .desktop file
PathAdd Wren to PATHthe program's folder in HKCU\Environment\Pathnot provided
Icons--the hicolor icons

PATH: the value stays a REG_EXPAND_SZ, entries are compared after expanding %VARIABLES% (case, slash direction and a trailing separator do not matter), the folder is never added twice, and open programs are told (WM_SETTINGCHANGE "Environment"). The value PathDir under Software\FromentSoftware\Wren says which folder Wren added: an entry the user put there by hand is never taken out (except the folder of a copy that is being uninstalled).

The Path part also holds wren.com, the console launcher that makes wren ctl ... work in a terminal (console-launcher.md): Options.launcher carries its bytes (the shell passes the ones embedded in wren.exe), install writes it beside the executable with the PATH entry and takes it away without it, remove and the uninstall delete it, and the Path part is "incomplete" (Repair) while the entry is there and the launcher is not. A file of that name without the launcher's mark is never replaced or deleted.

#Setup: the installed copy

src/desktop/install.odin (platform agnostic) and src/browser/setup.odin, setup_ui.odin (the dialog).

  • Where: %LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\Wren\wren.exe (Wren Dev for the development channel), or any folder that passes check_install_dir: an absolute path on a local drive, no forbidden character, not a drive root, not inside Windows, Program Files or ProgramData, not too long, and a file can be written in the nearest folder that exists (probe, nothing is created). On Linux: $XDG_DATA_HOME/wren.
  • What: the executable, named wren.exe in the install folder, and the manifest wren_install.txt (version, channel, every file). The release is the program alone (its licenses, its version and the C runtime are in it), so there is nothing else to copy; SETUP_PAYLOAD can list names beside the running executable that are copied when they exist. The demos and the test server are the separate extras archive: they are not installed.
  • Where the installed copy is: the Settings > Apps record, Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Uninstall\Wren (name, version, publisher, InstallLocation, icon, UninstallString = "<exe>" --setup), else the default folder.
  • Replacing a copy that runs: Windows lets a running program's file be renamed, not overwritten: each file already there is moved to <name>.old, the new one is written, and the .old files are removed (now if nothing holds them, else at the next start of the installed copy).
  • Uninstall: the parts (shortcuts, PATH entry, registration), the record, exactly the files of the manifest, the folders that become empty, the install folder when nothing else is in it. A manifest edited by hand cannot reach outside its folder. The running copy's own file is renamed aside, and a hidden cmd.exe batch file in %TEMP% (started when Wren ends) waits for the process, deletes it and the manifest, removes the folder and deletes itself.
  • The profile is never touched by an uninstall (bookmarks, history, settings stay).

States of the dialog (read from the disk by a job of the blocking pool): Not installed, Running installed, Running another copy (a copy is installed elsewhere; same version or newer: Replace installed copy), Older than installed, Repair (this is the installed copy but a shortcut, a key, the manifest or a file is missing or runs another executable).

#When it opens

  • The command Setup... (main menu, palette, a button beside the box in about:config) and wren.exe --setup: always.
  • At the start of a release copy that is not the installed one (browser.desktop_integration.on_first_run), and when the installed copy needs repair: never for development builds, --profile profiles, profiles in the temporary folder, portable copies, or with WREN_DESKTOP_INTEGRATION=off (tools\test_env.ps1 sets it for every script).
  • The profile remembers the answer in setup.txt: Use standalone (choice=standalone) is for good; closing the dialog without an answer (X, Escape, a click outside) is choice=dismissed and holds for the current version only.

#Standalone and portable

Standalone is a copy that was not installed and keeps the normal profile (%APPDATA%\Wren). A portable copy is a folder with a file wren.portable next to wren.exe: its profile (preferences, cookies, history, session, crash reports, licence) is <folder>\data, it never offers Setup by itself, and --profile DIR still wins.

#Updates

browser.update.check_daily (off: no request is made unless asked): one GET a day of GitHub's latest release (browser.update.url), compared with the running version, announced once per version; nothing is downloaded. The command Check for updates asks at once and opens the release page. State in update.txt in the profile. Never for disposable profiles or with WREN_UPDATE_CHECK=off.

#Following the disk

The state is read from the disk, never from a preference. On Windows one named thread (wren-desktop-watch) waits for the system to say that a place of the integration changed: the registry subtree HKCU\Software (registration, Uninstall entry), HKCU\Environment (PATH), the Start menu's Programs folder and the Desktop folder (the shortcuts). A change flags the state and wakes the browser: the box in about:config reads it again when shown, and an open Setup dialog reads it again (its state and badge follow what Settings > Apps, another Wren or a script did; the boxes being edited do not move). While the watcher runs nothing reads the disk on a timer; without one (a platform without a watcher, or a profile of its own: --profile, a temporary profile, WREN_DESKTOP_INTEGRATION=off) browser.desktop_integration.status_refresh_ms is the period. Coming back to the window reads the box's state at once.

#Command line

wren --desktop-integration=install|remove|status|uninstall, without a window. Exit codes: install and remove 0 done / 1 failed; status 0 installed / 1 absent / 2 to repair / 3 unreadable. The program is a Windows GUI program: to get the exit code, run it with Start-Process -Wait -PassThru (or start /wait); its output goes to a redirected standard output, else to the parent's console. It applies the preferences below (what the last Setup chose).

wren --uninstall [--purge] is the shorthand for --desktop-integration=uninstall: it removes the whole installed copy silently — the integration (shortcuts, the browser registration), the PATH entry, the Settings > Apps record and the files Setup placed — and keeps the user's profile unless --purge is given (which also deletes the profile: preferences, history, cookies, session, crash reports, licence). Exit codes: 0 done, 1 failed, 5 done but some files are in use and are removed when the running copy closes (the one being uninstalled is the one running). remove takes away only the integration; uninstall takes away the installed copy. --install is the shorthand for --desktop-integration=install.

#Preferences

browser.desktop_integration.on_first_run, .status_refresh_ms, .start_menu, .desktop_shortcut, .add_to_path, .register_browser (also register as a browser, or only the menu entry), .file_types, browser.update.check_daily, browser.update.url.

#Tests

odin test src/desktop runs the backend and the installed copy on scratch folders and a scratch registry key (HKCU\Software\WrenTest\<id>, deleted afterwards), and, on Linux, on scratch directories. odin test src/browser has the states of the dialog and install -> every state -> uninstall on scratch roots. A run can be pointed at scratch roots by the environment too: WREN_DESKTOP_MENU_DIR, WREN_DESKTOP_DESKTOP_DIR, WREN_DESKTOP_REGISTRY_ROOT, WREN_DESKTOP_ENVIRONMENT_ROOT (the key that stands for HKCU\Environment), WREN_DESKTOP_INSTALL_DIR (Windows), WREN_DESKTOP_APPLICATIONS_DIR, WREN_DESKTOP_ICONS_DIR (Linux). tools\setup_e2e.ps1 drives the real dialog of a built wren.exe on such a scratch desktop (install with Enter, uninstall of the running copy and its deferred deletion, standalone, the automatic opening and its exceptions, a portable copy) and compares the real Start menu, PATH, StartMenuInternet and Settings > Apps before and after. The one test that touches the real desktop runs only with WREN_TEST_DESKTOP_REAL=1 and uses an identity of its own.

#One Wren per profile

src/instance, src/browser/instance_shell.odin. The first Wren of a channel and a profile owns it (a named mutex Local\WrenInstance.Wren.<channel>.<hash of the profile folder> and a message-only window titled with that key); a second start hands its addresses (wren.exe <address or path>...: paths become file: addresses by the command line's rules), --setup and the request to come forward to it with WM_COPYDATA, after AllowSetForegroundWindow, and ends with exit code 0 before it has a window (about 30 ms). The first opens a tab per address, restores its window if minimized and takes the foreground. Nothing is done per frame.

CaseWhat happens
another profile, another channelindependent: each has its own key
another executable on the same profile (a newer download)it answers "another copy": that one opens its own window (Setup can replace the installed copy while it runs)
the first one has no window yet (starting) or refuses (closing)the second start tries again for up to 3 s; once the mutex is free it becomes the owner
the first one does not answer (busy, hung)after 3 s the second start opens its own window and says so (a notice, a line in the console)
--new-window, --no-single-instancea window of its own, once
browser.single_instance off, WREN_SINGLE_INSTANCE=offnever (=on forces it, for the script that checks it)
browser.profile.persist offnever: its folder is the user's, shared with a Wren that keeps it

tools\test_env.ps1 sets WREN_SINGLE_INSTANCE=off for every script that starts the browser, so none can hand its address to the user's Wren and end. tools\instance_e2e.ps1 checks the table on real processes and scratch profiles; tools\instance_startup.ps1 measures the cost of a start (one CreateMutexW: no measurable difference of the first present).
